chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Bashar, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdillah al-Dahqan, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Musa ibn Ja'far (AS), from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever sweeps a mosque on Thursday, the eve of Friday, and removes from it a speck of dust that could enter one's eye, he is forgiven.

key_terms.غُفِرَ لَهُ: He is forgiven — divine forgiveness as reward for the deed
key_terms.كَنَسَ: To sweep, to clean — specifically the act of cleaning a mosque
key_terms.مَا يُذَرُّ فِي الْعَيْنِ: An idiomatic expression meaning an extremely small amount, a speck (literally: what could be blown into the eye)
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ لَيْلَةَ الْجُمُعَةِ: Thursday, the eve of Friday — a blessed night in Islam

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for sweeping a mosque on Thursday night according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declared that sweeping a mosque on Thursday night — the eve of the blessed Friday — earns divine forgiveness, even if one removes only the smallest speck of dust. This hadith encourages the care and maintenance of mosques as an act of worship, with the specific timing of Thursday evening highlighting the sanctity of the Friday gathering. The Arabic idiom 'what is sprinkled in the eye' (ما يذر في العين) denotes an extremely minute quantity, emphasizing that even the smallest act of service to the mosque earns God's mercy.
